what: Merge Images joins several pictures into one file. Place them side by side, stack them top to bottom, or arrange them in a grid with as many columns as you like.
Pictures of different sizes can be scaled to match, so the result looks tidy. You choose the space between pictures, an outer border and the background colour, which can also be see-through.
Everything happens in your browser, so your pictures are never uploaded.
uses: Show two photos next to each other for a renovation, haircut or edit.
Stack several screenshots top to bottom to share a whole chat or web page.
Put product photos in a neat grid for a shop or presentation.
Combine photos from an event into one picture.
Join the front and back of an ID card or receipt into one image.
Collect colour or style examples in a grid.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop images here" and choose two or more files. Add more at any time.
Use ↑ and ↓ next to each name to move it, and ✕ to remove it.
"Side by side", "Top to bottom" or "Grid". For a grid, set "Columns in the grid".
"Make them the same size" scales every picture to match the largest or the smallest. In a grid, "Grid cells" shows each whole picture or fills each cell by trimming the edges.
Set "Space between" and "Outer border" in pixels and pick a background colour, or tick "See-through".
Choose "Save as" and press "Merge and download". The result size is shown above the button.
features: Side by side, top to bottom, or a grid with any number of columns.
Scale to the largest or smallest picture, or keep the original sizes.
Every cell has the same shape; show whole pictures or fill the cells.
Up to 200 px space and border, any background colour or see-through.
Move pictures up and down with large buttons that work on phones.
Results are kept to a size every phone can save.

example.title: Worked example: a before-and-after photo
example.text: Lucy painted her kitchen and has a before photo (4032 × 3024) and an after photo (3000 × 2250). She adds both, keeps "Side by side" and "Yes, match the largest", sets "Space between" to 20 px with a white background and saves as JPG. The result is 8084 × 3024 px; because that is over 16 megapixels it is reduced to about 6540 × 2446 px, still sharp enough for any screen.

tips: Choose "Match the smallest" if one picture is much smaller, so nothing is blown up and blurry.
For screenshots, stack them "Top to bottom" with no space for a seamless long image.
A 2-column grid with "Fill each cell" makes a neat collage from photos of different shapes.
Save as PNG for screenshots with text and JPG for photos.
problems: There are empty gaps in my grid
Pictures have different shapes. Choose "Fill each cell (trim edges)" in "Grid cells".
The result is smaller than the pictures
Results larger than about 16 megapixels are reduced so phones can save them. Merge fewer pictures, or match the smallest size.
JPG cannot be see-through. Choose PNG or WebP.
My iPhone photo will not open
Convert HEIC photos to JPG first with the HEIC to JPG tool.
